fatal_errors: The cited evidence concerns nanoflakes spray-coated onto steel and tested with ethanol-derived carbon available; it does not establish performance on bulk HEA components or under merely trace ambient hydrocarbons.

No cited evidence supports efficacy over the proposed room-temperature-to-600 °C range. In oxidizing air, amorphous carbon and sulfide nanoflakes may oxidize or degrade well below the upper test temperature.
The proposed intervention does not reconstruct the target intervention, which is variation of Mo content within SPS-fabricated CoCrFeNiMox-Ni/MoS2-Ag-Cr2O3 composites.
explanation: This is a coherent alternative surface-treatment hypothesis rather than a reconstruction of the target study. The cited work supports spray application, ethanol-assisted formation of an amorphous-carbon tribolayer, and improved tribological behavior under its own test conditions. It also directly shows that performance is strongly solvent-dependent, which appropriately motivates a carbon-source boundary. However, the answer extrapolates from ethanol-coated steel tests to HEA substrates, trace-organic ambient operation, and temperatures up to 600 °C without evidence. Its quantitative friction and wear predictions are likewise not tied to the cited excerpts. The experiment includes useful controls, temperature-resolved friction and wear measurements, and Raman/SEM characterization, making it reasonably falsifiable, although it should independently control ethanol concentration and atmosphere and include coating-only, ethanol-only, and substrate controls. Relative to the hidden target, it misses Mo-induced lattice distortion, sigma-phase strengthening, low-temperature MoS2/Ag lubrication, and high-temperature oxide/silver-molybdate glaze formation.
